interest: This document provides a concise record of early postwar Japanese maritime re-emergence following the end of the Allied Occupation, capturing the resumption of international training cruises to the Indian Ocean on the eve of the formal establishment of the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force in July 1954. It illustrates how the United States monitored Japanese naval diplomacy, port calls, and foreign contacts in newly independent South Asian nations like Ceylon (Sri Lanka).
overview: This file consists of a single State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet under decimal file 894.3346C, documenting visits of Japanese naval vessels to Ceylon in 1954. It indexes communication No. 166 dated June 26, 1954, sent by Foreign Service officer Livingston in Colombo to the Department of State (routed to the Bureau of Far Eastern Affairs and the Bureau of European Affairs), which reported on the routine training cruise port call of the Japanese vessels Itate and Asaka in Ceylon from June 18 to June 22, 1954.

subfiles.summary: This single-page List of Papers covers decimal file 894.3346C concerning visits of Japanese naval vessels to Ceylon. It records Sub No. 1, referencing Colombo communication No. 166 of June 26, 1954, from Livingston, distributed to FE, A-C/C, and WE. The entry reports that the Japanese vessels Itate and Asaka visited Ceylon from June 18 to June 22, 1954, as part of a routine training cruise.
